newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-WHITAKER TAKING A PEEK PAST HURTADO AT DE LA HOYA.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-WHITAKER TAKING A PEEK PAST HURTADO AT DE LA HOYA.

text.p: Pernell Whitaker couldn't help himself Wednesday, taking a peek past Friday's fight against Cuban exile Diobelis Hurtado at a possible titanic showdown against Oscar de la Hoya in April.

"I want to look spectacular, I want this fight to set the tone for what is ahead," Whitaker said of his scheduled 12-round defence of the World Boxing Council (WBC) welterweight belt at the Atlantic City Convention Centre.

Whitaker, 39-1-1, and the unbeaten de la Hoya have been moving toward a showdown for the last year. Last Friday de la Hoya did his part by keeping his WBC junior welterweight title by beating Mexican Miguel Angel Gonzalez.
Now it's Whitaker's turn and he intends on doing his part with de la Hoya at ringside. "He will get the message, see you on April 12," said Whitaker.
With de la Hoya as the prize, Whitaker is taking the lightly regarded Hurtado very seriously.

"There are obstacles ahead that are really motivating me to get me prepared this time," said Whitaker. "It's exciting. It made me go and prepare real well so that I make no mistakes out there to get to that point.
"I'm ready for all my skills to show. I'm ready to roll, ready to go, ready to put on a great show," Whitaker said.
Whitaker last fought four months ago by outpointing Wilfredo Rivera and wanted another fight before de la Hoya.
"I can't sit on my hands. I have to stay active," the 33-year-old Whitaker said.
Whitaker is risking a lot by meeting Hurtado, 20-0 since fleeing to the United States two years ago.
For this fight the champion's purse is $2 million according to his promoter Dino Duva. He is expected to get between $6-7 million to fight de la Hoya said Duva.

"I'm getting a little tired of everybody planning ahead, that Whitaker is just going to come here and blast this guy out of the water," Hurtado's promoter Luis DeCubas said. "They are making a big mistake."
There will be no mistakes, promised Whitaker.
"I don't know what kind of arsenel he has, I don't think it can stop me," Whitaker said of Hurtado, who had a 221-20 amateur record.
"This guy doesn't stand a chance against me because I'm so hyped, so excited and so prepared for him and the opportunity to get to the next level," Whitaker said.
